newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says Syria trying psychological pressure.
newsitem.headline: Israel says Syria trying psychological pressure.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday that Syria's troop redeployment in Lebanon was an attempt to pressure Israel into making unilateral territorial concessions.
"What Syria is trying to do is evidently to put psychological pressure on Israel and on its new government," Netanyahu told reporters after meeting parliament's Foreign Affairs and Defence Committee.

"It's not going to work. We are going to be careful and we're going to be prudent but we're not going to be pressured into making those unilateral concessions which perhaps Syria had become habituated to by the previous government," he said.
Syria has redeployed up to 12,000 troops in Lebanon, moving some within striking distance of a key Israeli position on the Golan Heights, causing war jitters in Israel.
"We are taking seriously all the signs on the ground. I am convinced we are taking all the necessary measures to defend the security of the country and its citizens," Netanyahu said.

The prime minister, who opposes trading occupied Arab land for peace and wants to hold on to all of the Golan, said Israel had sent messages to Syria through Egypt and the United States that its intentions are peaceful.
In addition, he said, Israel conveyed to Syria that "we are interested in resuming the diplomatic talks" stalled over the future of the Israeli-occupied Golan.
"As of this moment, we have yet to receive a clear answer from Syria about resuming talks," Netanyahu said.

U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross was due in the region on Tuesday to try to find a formula for restarting the negotiations broken off by Israel's previous Labour-led government after Moslem suicide bombings last February and March.
Syria has said it wants a commitment from Israel to quit all of the heights, captured in the 1967 Middle East war.

Commenting on the troop redeployment, Syrian Information Minister Mohammad Salman was quoted by the London-based al-Hayat newspaper on Tuesday as saying it was part of a continuous operation reflecting Syria's confidence in the increasing ability of Lebanese security forces.

But the newspaper quoted unidentified sources as saying the redeployment was linked to expectations in Damascus that Israel would launch a military campaign against pro-Iranian guerrillas in south Lebanon.
